description: My name is Illia Rybachyk. I’m a software engineer looking to build a unique, non-trivial project for the NASA Hackathon.
summary:
What we developed. "The Whisper of the Olive Branch" is an immersive Virtual Reality (VR) storytelling experience that transports users to the Sea of Tranquility in July 1969. Standing beside the Apollo 11 Lunar Module "Eagle", users discover the miniature golden olive branch left behind by the astronauts as a symbol of peace.
How it addresses the challenge. Instead of complex game mechanics, the experience relies on quiet contemplation and spatial 3D audio. Users simply gaze across the barren lunar surface, seeing the "Eagle" and the astronauts' footprints while hearing only their own breathing inside the spacesuit. Noticing the tiny golden olive branch invites deep reflection on its symbolism and the reality of life back on Earth—blending archival voices of world leaders from 1969 with the gentle heartbeat of our planet.
Why it is important. In a world still divided by conflict, this project harnesses the "Overview Effect" to remind humanity that when we look at our fragile home from afar, borders disappear—and peace remains our greatest shared mission.
details:
What it does and how it works
The Whisper of the Olive Branch is a short immersive VR story set on the Moon at the Apollo 11 landing site. The viewer stands on the lunar surface as an astronaut. They walk around the Lunar Module Eagle, follow the first footprints to the flag, and then come to a golden olive branch left in the dust. A narrated story, spacesuit breathing, a heartbeat, and music carry the viewer through the landing, the first step, and the mission’s message “in the interests of all humanity”. The story ends with a message about borders and unity, followed by recorded goodwill messages from around the world while Earth glows and pulses with the heartbeat above the horizon.
The experience starts from an interactive Moon in VR with a marker on the Apollo 11 site. Selecting it launches the story. It runs in the browser on Meta Quest 2 through WebXR and also works on a desktop with mouse look.
Benefits and intended impact
The project turns a historic event into a personal, emotional experience that anyone can open with a web link, with no app installation. It connects Apollo 11’s message of peace and shared humanity with today’s world, and it invites people to remember why we went to the Moon in the first place. It is aimed at students, museums, and general audiences interested in space history.
Tools and technology
React, three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, React Three XR (WebXR), GSAP for animation, Vite, and the Web Audio API. We used a 3D model of the Apollo 11 landing site and a Lunar Module model, a Moon-and-Earth texture set, and the real Apollo 11 bootprint photograph, processed into a ground-decal texture. Hardware: Meta Quest 2 for testing and a desktop browser.
What is creative about it
The story is told through atmosphere rather than text: we hear the astronaut’s breathing, and the narration is paced to the walk. Subtitles follow the viewer’s gaze, and the camera movement is slow and gentle. The Earth glows in the sky in rhythm with a heartbeat to make a distant planet feel alive and fragile. The golden olive branch gives a clear, simple symbol of peace.
Factors we considered
Comfort and accessibility: slow movement, no sudden camera motion, subtitles for all narration, and no need for controllers. Performance: Quest 2 has limited power, so we optimized models, textures, shadows, and the number of stars. Historical respect: real footprints and a real landing site. Flexibility: all story content (texts, timings, volumes) lives in one config file, so new missions or languages can be added easily.
